policy: A human-reviewed official link is usable for ordinary research within the identified publisher, instrument, language, displayed date, reviewed content, and limitations. BOE consolidated legislation is accepted as a government-published working text; BOE itself labels it informational and without legal value. For legal-effect, commencement, correction, or a known material post-cutoff issue, follow the specific linked official publication. Do not reconstruct a Gazette amendment chain as a routine prerequisite. API access, local capture, hashing, replay, conversion, and copying permission are not prerequisites for ordinary public-link use. Local copies and converted candidate files remain separately unaccepted. Source acceptance does not establish topic adequacy or country completion.

legacy_inventory.local_acceptance_note: Fifteen BOE law texts and thirty broader government pages were converted and replay-verified as candidate artifacts. None is accepted as a local copy. The separate register accepts 25 externally linked references within stated scopes; inaccessible or dynamic pages are handled through human-review site offers rather than treated as unusable sources.

es-50.publisher: Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE)

es-50.scope: The joint DGM/DGP instruction for issuing the Spanish residence document under Article 18.4 of the EU-UK Withdrawal Agreement, including covered UK nationals, family members and other persons, application routes and EX-20/EX-21 documents.
es-50.reviewed_content: The BOE record identifies the resolution and original instruction. The text states that Spain chose the Article 18.4 document model and sets out distinct procedures for UK nationals and qualifying third-country family members.
limitations: This is the closest official published text, not a consolidated version; check a specific later instruction or material legal change when relevant.
It does not by itself establish the full Withdrawal Agreement eligibility test or current provincial appointments, fees and forms.

es-51.publisher: Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration, Spain

es-51.reviewed_content: The page distinguishes Withdrawal Agreement beneficiaries from post-transition arrivals, states Spain chose Article 18.4, links the BOE instruction, and links the Spanish-language family guide.
limitations: The page and linked guide still describe EES and ETIAS rollout dates as future events in 2024/2025; do not rely on those time-sensitive statements for current border procedures.
Current eligibility, forms, filing channels and appointment arrangements need issue-specific checking against the current official route.

es-52.publisher: Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration, Spain

es-52.reviewed_content: The cover and contents identify the publisher and date. Relevant sections describe existing and later-joining family members, document procedures and the Article 50 TUE residence card.
limitations: This is nonbinding Ministry guidance, not legislation; use it with the Withdrawal Agreement and the BOE-published instruction.
Its EES and ETIAS timing statements are stale as of this review date; check current border-system rules separately.
The September 2024 guide may not reflect later changes to law or administrative practice.

not_accepted_candidate_notes: Local BOE and broader-page conversions remain candidates; the link decisions above do not accept those files.

The EU-UK Withdrawal Agreement current-consolidation link is identified but not counted as accepted pending human inspection through EUR-Lex; the official site is offered above.
